text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Causeway toll charges are likely to go up when Tuas link between Singapore and Johor opens on January 2.
- Singapore faces shortfall of about 7,000 graduates a year from 2000 and has to take pro-active steps to make up the numbers, says Deputy Prime Minister Tony Tan in Parliament.
- Parliament approves government's overall budget for year, after more than 40 hours of debate.
- Three robbers caught soon after breaking into house in Yio Chu Kang because of T-shirt they left behind near scene of crime.
- Interim corporate reporting season here again, but do not hope for listed companies' earnings to lift sluggish stock market, because even top 12 companies may not come up winners.
- Singapore Telecom enters into memorandum of understanding with Telephone Organisation of Thailand, paving way for future investment in Thai monopoly.

- National Development Ministry says it is studying letter of appeal by property developers to curb government land sales, and points out it does not have any fixed target on supply of private housing.

- Malaysian government will step in and appoint new contractor for massive Bakun dam if developer and main contractor fail to resolve dispute over main building contract, says Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
- Stock Exchange of Thailand backs out of plan to allow greater volatility in share trading, move analysts said reflects fears of unstable market in current weak economic climate.
- Billionaire financier George Soros funded Russian government budget short-falls on several occasions, in particular in interval between recent Eurobond issues, says former top government official.

- Diversified telecommunications firm Acma Ltd ends speculation surrounding fate of US associate Hayes Microcomputer Products by announcing Hayes has finally managed to gain backdoor listing on Nasdaq.
- UOB subsidiary Industrial & Commercial Bank announces slightly better interim profits while earnings at insurance arm United Overseas Insurance dented by lacklustre stock market.

- Pacific Can Investment Holdings has agreed to acquire a Malaysian property company for Singapore $11.56 million, paving way for can-making-cum-construction company to diversify into property investment and development.
- DBS Land adding another piece of history to hotel portfolio with S$64 million deal to buy 100-year-old Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten in Hamburg.
